title: {mate}'s slate
goals: {familiar} and {mate_familiar} in the circle, each with its name and its colour.
starting_code:
class {familiar_class}(Familiar):
    def __init__(name, color):
        name = name
        color = color

{familiar_var} = {familiar_class}("{familiar}", "{familiar_color}")
{mate_var} = {familiar_class}("{mate_familiar}", "{mate_color}")
wizard.cast("minka", {familiar_var})
wizard.cast("minka", {mate_var})
hints: The first thing `__init__` takes is always the object being born.
With `self` in its place, the trials come with no name: `name = name` keeps the name only inside the action, not in the object.
Two fixes: `self` first between the brackets of `__init__`, and `self.` before the two names that are kept.
intro:
I give up: I'm hopeless at this, not one of mine comes out right. Let me copy your description, and I'll have a familiar just like yours, but in another colour.

I copied yours onto my slate in a hurry and added my own line. Mine will be called *(softly)* {mate_familiar}. You'd better do the conjuring too: nothing works for me today.
outro: One class, and two familiars, each with its name and its colour. Thank you, {wizard}!
learned: Now you know the two slips everyone makes with a class: one Python tells you about, a missing `self`, and one nobody tells you about, a name kept only inside the action; and that one class makes as many objects as needed, each with its own data.
